purpose: Gemfibrozil is used to lower high triglycerides (a type of fat in your blood) and raise your good cholesterol (HDL). It helps reduce your risk of heart disease, especially if diet and exercise alone have not been enough. Your doctor may prescribe it when other cholesterol medications are not right for you.
how_it_works: Gemfibrozil works in your liver to slow down the production of triglycerides and help your body break them down faster. It also helps raise your good cholesterol (HDL), which protects your heart. Think of it as helping your body clean up the unhealthy fats circulating in your blood.
common_side_effects: Stomach upset, nausea, diarrhea, or stomach pain are the most common issues. Some people feel dizzy or get headaches. You may also notice muscle aches, which is important to report to your doctor right away.
warnings: Do not take gemfibrozil with certain cholesterol medications called statins (like simvastatin or lovastatin) unless your doctor specifically approves it, as this combination can cause serious muscle damage. Tell your doctor if you have kidney, liver, or gallbladder problems, as this medicine is not safe in those situations. Contact your doctor immediately if you have unusual muscle pain, weakness, or dark-colored urine.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 600 mg taken twice a day, about 30 minutes before your morning and evening meals. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
